title_ar: الحض على صلاة الصبح في المسجد
title_en: Urging the Dawn Prayer in the Mosque
body_ar:
بم تنصحون من تفوته صلاة الصبح في الجماعة دائما؟

أن على هذا الإنسان أن يتذكر أنها صلاة المنافقين، وأن أصحاب النبي (ص) كانوا يعرفون نفاق الرجل بتخلفه عن الجماعة في صلاة الصبح، إذا كان لا يشهد صلاة العشاء والفجر في الجماعة حكموا بنفاقه وعرفوا أنه من المنافقين، ولذلك لا بد أن نحرص على أدائها في الجماعة، وأن نعلم أن من أدى هاتين الصلاتين في الجماعة كان في ذمة الله فلا يطلبنكم الله من ذمته بشيء، ومن أداهما في الجماعة كتب له قيام ليلة ونصف ليلة، فعلى الإنسان أن يحرص وبالأخص إذا عرف أن جزاء المشي في الظلام إلى صلاة الفجر النور التام يوم القيامة: «بشر المشائين في سدف الليل إلى المساجد بالنور التام يوم القيامة»، فلذلك علينا أن نحرص جميعا شبابا وشيبا على شهود صلاة الفجر في الجماعة، وأن نتذكر قول الله تعالى: {وَقُرْآَنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآَنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا}، فهو مشهود يشهده نوعان من أنواع الملائكة، ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار: «يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار يجتمعون في صلاة العصر وصلاة الفجر».
body_en:
What do you counsel someone who always misses the dawn prayer in congregation?

This person must remember that it is the prayer of the hypocrites, and that the Companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to recognise a man's hypocrisy by his staying away from the congregation at the dawn prayer: if he did not attend the night prayer and the dawn prayer in congregation, they judged him to be a hypocrite and knew that he was one of the hypocrites. For that reason we must be diligent in performing it in congregation, and must know that whoever performs these two prayers in congregation is under God's guarantee — so let God not call on you for anything from His guarantee. And whoever performs both of them in congregation, the standing in prayer of a night and of half a night is written for him. So a person must be diligent, and especially when he knows that the reward for walking in the darkness to the dawn prayer is complete light on the Day of Resurrection: 'Give glad tidings to those who walk much in the darknesses of the night to the mosques, of complete light on the Day of Resurrection.' Therefore we must all be diligent, young and old, in attending the dawn prayer in congregation, and must remember the words of God, exalted: {and the recitation of the dawn — truly the recitation of the dawn is witnessed} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:78). It is witnessed: two kinds of angels witness it, the angels of the night and the angels of the day — 'Angels take turns among you by night and angels by day, and they gather at the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer.'

flags.arabic: أن يتذكر أنها صلاة المنافقين … حكموا بنفاقه وعرفوا أنه من المنافقين
flags.context: the opening of the Sheikh's counsel
options: render literally, keeping the Companions' practice as a reported historical practice
render as a ruling that one who misses the dawn prayer is a hypocrite
soften to 'a sign of weak faith'
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, AND A CAREFUL DISTINCTION. The Sheikh is asked for counsel, not for a ruling, and what he gives is exhortation: he says the person should REMEMBER that this is the prayer of the hypocrites, and reports what the Companions used to infer. He does not himself rule that a man who misses the dawn prayer is a hypocrite, and the English must not let him. Equally, the language must not be softened into 'a sign of weak faith', which is not what he said. Read in English out of context, a passage classing absentees from a dawn prayer as hypocrites carries obvious reputational risk; it has been translated faithfully and the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: فلا يطلبنكم الله من ذمته بشيء
flags.context: within the Sheikh's paraphrase of a report about God's guarantee
options: so let God not call on you for anything from His guarantee
so let God not hold you accountable for any breach of His guarantee
flags.note: This clause is part of the wording of a well-known report and is elliptical in Arabic: the sense is a warning against breaking the guarantee one has entered into, not a supplication. The Sheikh slips from his own voice into the report's wording without marking the transition, so the boundary between his words and the report is lost in the source. The English keeps the clause where the source puts it and does not mark it as a quotation. He gives no narrator, collection or grading for it and none has been supplied.

flags.arabic: «بشر المشائين في سدف الليل …» … «يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل …»
flags.context: the two reports quoted in the second half
options: quote as the Sheikh gives them, with no attribution or grading
flags.note: Both reports are given in quotation marks with no narrator, no collection and no grading, and nothing has been supplied. The first is the only one of the four reports in this record that the source marks as a quotation at all; the claims about God's guarantee and about the reward of standing a night in prayer are given in the Sheikh's own voice although they too are report wordings. A reviewer may wish the site to mark them.

The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The source writes the eulogy after the Prophet's name sometimes in full and sometimes as the abbreviation (ص). Both are rendered as 'peace and blessings be upon him'; the source form is preserved in body_ar.
The Qur'anic quotation is given in the source fully vowelled and without a reference; the reference has been supplied per house style. The wording matches the closing clause of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:78.
'Complete light' renders al-nūr al-tāmm, the report's own phrase, and 'the darknesses of the night' renders sudaf al-layl.
The source spells المشائين; preserved in body_ar.
